home_title: Cicada: live subtitles, interpreting and meeting notes for any call or stream | Free for Mac
home_desc: Cicada is a Mac menu bar app for live translated subtitles, push-to-talk interpreting and AI meeting notes. Works in Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, X Spaces, YouTube Live and Discord, with no bot in the call. Audio stays on your Mac. Free and open source.

why_h:
Teams and Meet have captions?
Only inside their own apps.
why_lead: X Spaces, YouTube Live, Discord and podcasts don’t. Cicada listens to everything your Mac plays: no bot joins the call, and nobody else installs anything.
c1_b: Only in that app’s own meetings
c1_u: Any app, any web page, any stream
c2_b: The host turns it on, often on a paid plan
c2_u: You turn it on yourself; nobody else is affected
c3_u: Hold right ⌥ and speak; they hear their language
v1_p: What others say turns into subtitles in your language as they speak. It works out which language they’re speaking; speech recognition runs entirely on your Mac.
v2_p: Hold right ⌥ and talk. When you let go, it’s translated into their language and spoken through a virtual microphone. Works in any app you can speak in.
v3_p: Notes written while the meeting runs: key points, decisions, to-dos and “what did I miss”. Afterwards you keep a bilingual record, exportable to Markdown, Word and SRT.
fine: Subtitles work everywhere; interpreting needs a place where you can speak, like a call or a Space. AI notes and natural voices use your own Ling key, which comes with ¥10 of free credit every month.
cta_h: In your next meeting, Cicada listens, speaks and remembers for you.
cta_p: They talk, you read subtitles in your language; you talk, they hear theirs; the meeting is turned into notes as it goes, and you keep a bilingual record. Audio is turned into text only on your Mac.

p1_h: Audio becomes text on your Mac
p1_p: Recordings and meeting records stay on your own disk. The only things sent out are the recognized text (for translation and notes) and, when you use interpreting, the few sentences you speak while holding the key.
p2_h: Asked only when needed, optional where possible
p2_p: System audio is for subtitles; the microphone records only while you hold the talk key; Input Monitoring only watches the right ⌥ (not needed with a key combination). The notes window stays hidden when you share your screen.
p3_p: It only connects to the translation service, your own Ling key, the official BlackHole download and GitHub. No analytics and no servers of our own. Installers can be checked against their SHA-256.
r1_h: Record what I say, tell speakers apart
r1_p: What you say in the meeting goes into the notes too. Support back to macOS 14.4. Proper signing, so no more “Open Anyway” on first launch. Several speakers on the other side told apart, with to-dos showing who said them. Notes written by an on-device model, with no key needed.
r2_p: Remember the voices of colleagues you meet often and recognize them next time; voiceprints stay on your Mac. A full version for Windows. Android can’t capture call audio, so it starts with subtitles for videos and streams, a face-to-face mode and a meeting record viewer.
